reader.requirement: At --std 85, in CALL ... USING, a BY CONTENT or BY REFERENCE phrase (BY optional) applies to every following identifier-2 until the next such phrase, and arguments before any phrase are passed BY REFERENCE; the 1985 USING admits only identifier-2 operands under those two phrases, so BY VALUE, OMITTED and literal operands are refused.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry program-prototype-name-2002: false at 85, so BindCall takes the judgedUpFront arm (every argument's spelling judged before binding, carried mode threaded by CallArgumentModes.CarriedAfter)
ConstructRegistry availability of each Format-2-only spelling (BY VALUE, OMITTED, literal/expression operand): refused COBOL0900 at 85, admitted at 2023
ConstructRegistry call-function-identifier-argument-2002 (the 1985 SR4 refusal of a function-identifier operand) in the up-front arm

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: 2023 adds BY VALUE (also transitive) and literal/OMITTED operands; at 85 those are refused, and the transitive mode itself (CallArgumentModes.CarriedAfter over WrittenPhrase, the one writer, kb/Work PB3227) is the same code at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb131 covers BY CONTENT A B BY REFERENCE C D with BY written; it does not exercise the bare leading default before a later phrase, the BY-less REFERENCE/CONTENT spelling, a subordinate elementary operand, or the refusal of 2002 operand forms.

probes.expected: all by reference with no phrase; USING REFERENCE A CONTENT B C REFERENCE D CONTENT G1 changes only A and D; USING A BY CONTENT B BY REFERENCE C BY CONTENT D G1 changes only A (assumed BY REFERENCE) and C

probes.printed: error COBOL0900: the CALL BY VALUE phrase requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: refused: the 1985 format has only BY REFERENCE and BY CONTENT

probes.printed: error COBOL0900: a literal or expression as a CALL argument requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: refused: BY CONTENT takes identifier-2 only in 1985

probes.printed: error COBOL0900: the omitted-argument facility (OMITTED / OPTIONAL / IS OMITTED) requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: refused: OMITTED is not in the 1985 format

reader.notes: Re-read at 29fac30622 after kb/Work PB3227 moved the carried-mode writer from CallBinder.CarriedModeAfter to CallArgumentModes.CarriedAfter (WrittenPhrase ?? carried: the same three-phrase test, unchanged). BindCall's up-front 85 judgement and its binding loop both thread the mode through it, starting from an initial BY REFERENCE; a Format-1 keyword-less identifier (KeywordLessIdentifier with formatTwo false) takes the carried mode. The stored probes re-run at this head (--std 85, runs under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/finish-worktree-wf_bd30c11f-c3a-20/runs) print what they printed at the first read: c1pos all three mixes as GR12 derives; c1val, c1lit, c1omit refused COBOL0900.

refuter.evidence: Re-ran at 29fac30622 (--std 85, runs under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/finish-worktree-wf_bd30c11f-c3a-20/runs) the first refuter's probes (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-033/src): r3pos printed 'DYN A=0001 T2=0007 B=0012 T3=0017 G1=0015' / 'NOEXC' / 'LIT A=0001 B=0012 T1=0007 T2=0017 G1=0025', exactly as at 1df234fa72 (content and reference transitive over subscripted elements and a subordinate item, on the identifier-1 and the literal paths). Degenerate forms still refused: r3n1 'USING BY CONTENT BY REFERENCE A' COBOL0001 unexpected 'BY'; r3n2 COBOL0001 unexpected '.'; r3n3 'USING BY REFERENCE' now COBOL5506 (the separator period ends the CALL where an operand is due; main's parse-diagnostic wording, same refusal); r3n4 'BY CONTENT ADDRESS OF A' COBOL0900; r3n5 'LENGTH OF A' COBOL5506. CallArgumentModes.CarriedAfter is the body CallBinder.CarriedModeAfter held (WrittenPhrase tests callByReference, callByContent, callByValue in that order, then the carried mode), so no edition site moved out of the read. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.5.2.4 GR12  (5.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR12'.
